Interface HttpRouteGroup

All Superinterfaces:
ExecutionSpec<HttpRouteGroup>, HttpRouteScope, RouteFilterSpec<HttpRouteGroup>, RouteSpec<HttpRouteGroup>
public sealed interface HttpRouteGroup extends HttpRouteScope, RouteSpec<HttpRouteGroup>
A group of routes, declared with HttpRouteScope.group(Consumer) or, under a prefix, with HttpRouteScope.path(String, Consumer): the routes declared on the group, and in the groups nested in it, are the routes of the group, and the filters of the group apply to each of them. 
routes.path("/api", api -> {
    api.GET("/orders", (request, pathVariables) -> HttpResponse.ok(orders.all()));
    api.path("/admin", admin -> {
        admin.GET("/users", (request, pathVariables) -> HttpResponse.ok(users.all()));
        admin.beforeReplacing(request -> isAdmin(request) ? null : HttpResponse.status(HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN));
    });
    api.beforeReplacing((request, propagatedContext) -> {
        propagatedContext.add(new MdcPropagationContext(Map.of("tenant", tenantOf(request))));
        return null;
    });
});

Coverage. A filter of the group applies to every route declared in the lambda of the group, wherever the filter is declared in it: before the routes, after them, or in between. The filters are resolved when the routes are built. The group is closed when its lambda returns: declaring a route or a filter on it afterwards fails.

Order. The server filters, the @ServerFilter beans and the filters declared with HttpRouteBuilder.serverFilter(String...), run first. Then the filters of the outer group, then those of the inner groups, then those of the route, then the handler. Response filters run the other way: the filters of the route, then those of the inner groups, then those of the outer group, then the application's response filters. Within a group or a route, request filters and response filters each run in the order they are declared, like the filters of a route.

Matched routes only. As with the filter methods of a controller, the filters of the group, the before and after families, are route filters: a filter of the group runs only when a route of the group matched the request. A request under the prefix of the group that no route answers, a 404, or one that a route of the group would answer with another method or media type, a 405, 415 or 406, does not run the filters of the group; a @ServerFilter("/api/**") bean, or a server filter declared with serverFilter("/api/**") on the builder, pre-matching or not, filters every request under a prefix, those responses included. A group declares no server filter: its filters are route filters, which apply to the routes of the group only.

Errors. An exception of a route of the group is answered by the error routes, and the response filters of the group, like those of the route, filter the response of the error route. The error and status routes declared on a group, HttpRouteScope.error(Class, ErrorRouteHandler), HttpRouteScope.errorAsync(Class, AsyncErrorRouteHandler), HttpRouteScope.status(HttpStatus, StatusRouteHandler) and HttpRouteScope.statusAsync(HttpStatus, AsyncStatusRouteHandler), are local to the routes of the group and of its nested groups, like the @Error methods of a controller that are not global: the error of a route is answered by an error route of its innermost group, then of the groups around it, then by a global one, declared on the builder of an HttpRoutes bean or on a controller with global = true. A request no route of the group matched, e.g. a 404 under the prefix of the group, is answered by the global error and status routes only.

Settings. A group has every setting of a route, see RouteSpec, but its response type: the media types, the executor, the port, the conditions, the order, the attributes, the annotations and the annotated element of a group, see RouteSpec.consumes(MediaType...), ExecutionSpec.executeOn(String), RouteSpec.port(int), RouteSpec.annotationMetadata(AnnotationMetadataProvider) and the others, apply to the routes declared in the lambda of the group, and of its nested groups, wherever they are declared in the lambda, like its filters. A route, or a nested group, with its own value overrides the one of the group. The media types, the executor and the annotated element apply to the routes to handlers, not to the locator routes of the group.

Locators. A locator route declared in a group is under the prefix of the group, and the filters of the group apply to every located route, before the filters of the located route.

Pending routes. A route declared on the group is ended with a terminal, see HttpRouteSpec, in the lambda of the group: a route of the group with no terminal when the lambda returns fails with an IllegalStateException naming it.
